[Pedagogy review · High priority · opening-review · pf-745d44e9b0]
Before p3-general-form, add: (a) Factorise x²-7x+10. (b) Factorise x²+x-12. (c) For y=x²-6x+5, write the substituted expression and find y when x=2. (d) For y=x²+4x-12, write the substituted expression and find y when x=-3. Answers: (a) (x-5)(x-2); (b) (x+4)(x-3); (c) 2²-6(2)+5=-3; (d) (-3)²+4(-3)-12=-15. Keep the review within one page.
Also affects: p5-example-demonstration

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-29fab67b67]
At p12-q10-a: After part b add: (i) Find the x-intercepts of y=-2x²-12x-16. Answer: (-4,0), (-2,0). (ii) Find its vertex. Answer: (-3,2). (iii) Find its y-intercept. Answer: (0,-16). (iv) Sketch it. Answer: concave down through these features. (v) Explain why it has the same x-intercepts as parts a and b. Answer: each equation is a nonzero multiple of (x+4)(x+2).
Also relates to: p12-q10-b

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · variation-sequence · pf-3f55afaf4d]
At p30-q1: Add one instruction: “Predict the number of x-intercepts before completing the square.” Append (f) y=x²-4x+3; (g) y=x²-4x+4; (h) y=x²-4x+5. Answers: (x-2)²-1, vertex (2,-1), roots 1 and 3, y-intercept 3; (x-2)², vertex and root (2,0), y-intercept 4; (x-2)²+1, vertex (2,1), no roots, y-intercept 5. Follow with unpatterned (i) y=x²+2x-2: (x+1)²-3, vertex (-1,-3), roots -1±√3, y-intercept -2. All are concave up.
